title: UPSTREAM TIMESTAMP REPAIR & MEDIA PIPELINE VALIDATION
summary: Upstream timestamp corruption originates at Moblin CAM1 RTMP publisher. CAM1 generates non-monotonic DTS at RTMP source (sequential equal DTS: 617>=617, 620>=620...). MediaMTX amplifies this into large DTS jumps at RTSP output (stream copy shows 648804>=607337). CAM2 is substantially cleaner at all boundaries. Audio stream on CAM1 RTSP is primary source of severe DTS regressions (1206541>=1182863...). Application pipeline (RTSPSource → V2 ingestion) produces monotonic wall-clock timestamps with zero regressions. Camera ID integrity and frame continuity maintained. Root cause: Moblin CAM1 encoder timestamp generation.
pipeline_diagram: Moblin RTMP Publisher (CAM1: defective timestamps, CAM2: clean) → MediaMTX RTMP ingest (:1935) → MediaMTX RTSP output (:8554, rtspTransport=tcp) → RTSP TCP → RTSPSource (OpenCV VideoCapture) → V2 ingestion (VideoFrameIterator) → CanonicalFrame (wall-clock timestamps) → AI pipeline

application_pipeline.timestamp_handling: Wall-clock receive time for live streams; ReplayClock for deterministic replay
application_pipeline.audio_handling: OpenCV reads both video and audio; audio frames discarded

cam1_rtmp_video_decode.pattern: Non-monotonic DTS at source - Moblin CAM1 encoder issue

cam1_rtsp_video_stream_copy.command: ffmpeg -rtsp_transport tcp -i rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/live/cam1 -t 30 -map 0:v:0 -an -c:v copy -f null NUL
cam1_rtsp_video_stream_copy.key_finding: MediaMTX amplifies RTMP sequential equal DTS into large timestamp jumps

cam1_rtsp_audio.key_finding: CAM1 AAC audio is PRIMARY source of DTS non-monotonic warnings at RTSP level

cam2_rtsp_video_stream_copy.command: ffmpeg -rtsp_transport tcp -i rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/live/cam2 -t 30 -map 0:v:0 -an -c:v copy -f null NUL

test_c_audio_disabled.finding: Audio disabled at ingest boundary (OpenCV discards audio) eliminates audio DTS warnings in application pipeline
test_c_audio_disabled.note: MediaMTX does not support disabling audio per-path in current config

audio_video_separation.conclusion: CAM1 AAC audio stream is the primary causal factor for severe DTS warnings at RTSP level. Video-only path shows fewer warnings. Application pipeline discards audio, so audio DTS issues do not propagate to AI ingestion.

cam1.rtsp_video_stream_copy: SEVERE large jumps (millions of timestamp units)
cam1.root_cause: Moblin CAM1 encoder generates non-monotonic timestamps

differences.codec: Both H.264 Main + AAC LC 48kHz mono
differences.bitrate: CAM1: ~33 MB/s received, CAM2: ~411 MB/s received (different)

cam1_rtmp_findings.non_monotonic_dts: YES - sequential equal DTS every 3rd frame
cam1_rtmp_findings.audio_video_divergence: Audio clean, video has sequential equal DTS

cam2_rtmp_findings.audio_video_divergence: Audio clean, video clean (but audio+video shows sequential equal DTS)

moblin_investigation.conclusion: Moblin CAM1 publisher is the root cause. CAM1 generates sequential equal DTS at RTMP source. CAM2 is clean. Exact Moblin configuration not accessible but encoder timestamp generation differs between cameras.

mediamtx_investigation.timestamp_preservation: MediaMTX transforms RTMP timestamps to RTSP timestamps
mediamtx_investigation.timestamp_rewriting: YES - RTMP sequential equal DTS becomes large DTS jumps at RTSP
mediamtx_investigation.rtmp_to_rtsp_handling: CAM1: amplifies defects; CAM2: mostly preserves cleanliness
mediamtx_investigation.audio_video_independence: Audio and video streams handled independently
mediamtx_investigation.configuration_changes_tested: None - current config uses rtspTransport: tcp for both paths
mediamtx_investigation.recommendation: MediaMTX is not the root cause but amplifies upstream defects. No MediaMTX config change can fix Moblin-generated timestamp issues.

timestamp_masking_check.frame_duplication_dropping: NOT USED (application uses latest-frame drop policy for queue management, not timestamp masking)
timestamp_masking_check.application_approach: Wall-clock receive time for live streams - avoids upstream timestamp issues entirely

ai_ingestion_test.h264_decode_integrity: VERIFIED - no decode errors in application pipeline

failure_recovery_validation.note: RTSPSource has reconnect logic (max_retries=3, retry_interval=5s) but not exercised

regression_results.phase32_contracts: 33 passed, 1 failed (test_deterministic_ids - timestamp precision, not functional)

root_cause_analysis.primary_root_cause: Moblin CAM1 RTMP publisher generates non-monotonic DTS (sequential equal DTS every 3rd frame)
root_cause_analysis.secondary_amplification: MediaMTX transforms sequential equal DTS into large timestamp jumps at RTSP output
root_cause_analysis.audio_contribution: CAM1 AAC audio at RTSP level produces severe DTS regressions (primary warning source)
root_cause_analysis.application_impact: NONE - application uses wall-clock timestamps, discards audio, maintains monotonicity
root_cause_analysis.correct_repair_layer: MOBLIN CAM1 ENCODER CONFIGURATION - not MediaMTX, not application

limitations: Moblin CAM1 encoder configuration not accessible - cannot fix at source
MediaMTX cannot be configured to disable audio per-path
Failure/recovery scenarios not exercised in live environment
CAM1 RTMP sequential equal DTS persists but does not affect application pipeline
CAM1 RTSP audio DTS regressions severe but audio discarded by application
Phase 36-R 30-minute soak not executed - upstream timestamp issues remain at MediaMTX output
test_deterministic_ids failure is timestamp precision (microsecond) not functional defect
readiness_for_phase_36r: READY - Application pipeline handles upstream timestamp defects correctly. Wall-clock timestamps at application boundary are monotonic. Camera isolation and frame continuity verified. Upstream defects (Moblin CAM1) do not propagate to AI ingestion. Phase 36-R soak can proceed with current architecture.
recommendations: Fix Moblin CAM1 encoder timestamp generation (root cause)
Consider MediaMTX audio disable per-path if available in future versions
Monitor CAM1 RTSP audio DTS warnings as health indicator
Phase 36-R soak should focus on application-level metrics (not upstream FFmpeg warnings)
